headline: BEPZA announces major recruitment for 117 positions across 34 categories
summary: The Bangladesh Export Processing Zones Authority (BEPZA) has issued a job circular for 117 posts in grades 9 to 20. Applications will open on July 1, 2026, offering diverse career opportunities.
details: The Bangladesh Export Processing Zones Authority (BEPZA) has published a recruitment circular for 117 positions across 34 different categories, ranging from grade 9 to 20. The application process is set to begin on July 1, 2026.

These positions include Assistant Director (Administration, Investment, Accounts/Audit), Assistant Engineer (Civil, Electrical), Security Officer, Sub-Assistant Engineer, Librarian, Storekeeper, Office Assistant cum Computer Operator, Driver, Electrician, and Security Guard, among many others.

Interested candidates must apply online through the official BEPZA Teletalk website: http://bepza.teletalk.com.bd. Detailed information about specific roles and eligibility criteria can be found on the website.

The application submission and fee payment window opens on July 1, 2026, at 10:00 AM and closes on July 30, 2026, at 5:00 PM. Application fees vary by grade, ranging from 56 Taka to 223 Taka, including service charges.
caption:
Looking for a government job opportunity? BEPZA has announced a major recruitment drive for 117 positions across 34 categories!

The Bangladesh Export Processing Zones Authority (BEPZA) has published a recruitment circular for 117 positions across 34 different categories, ranging from grade 9 to 20. The application process is set to begin on July 1, 2026.

These positions include Assistant Director (Administration, Investment, Accounts/Audit), Assistant Engineer (Civil, Electrical), Security Officer, Sub-Assistant Engineer, Librarian, Storekeeper, Office Assistant cum Computer Operator, Driver, Electrician, and Security Guard, among many others.

Interested candidates must apply online through the official BEPZA Teletalk website: http://bepza.teletalk.com.bd. Detailed information about specific roles and eligibility criteria can be found on the website.

The application submission and fee payment window opens on July 1, 2026, at 10:00 AM and closes on July 30, 2026, at 5:00 PM. Application fees vary by grade, ranging from 56 Taka to 223 Taka, including service charges.

Source: Prothom Alo

headline_marked: Expatriates face [[endless suffering to bring home bodies]] of deceased
headline: Expatriates face endless suffering to bring home bodies of deceased
summary: Families of deceased expatriates struggle with bureaucratic hurdles and logistical challenges when repatriating remains from abroad.
details: Families of deceased expatriates are facing extreme difficulties and endless suffering while trying to bring the bodies of their loved ones back to Bangladesh.
The process of repatriation involves navigating complex bureaucratic hurdles and coordinating between different government agencies and embassies.
Families often report delays in the paperwork and a lack of clear guidance on the necessary legal requirements for transporting remains across borders.
These logistical challenges add significant emotional distress to families who are already grieving the loss of a member.

The situation highlights the need for a more streamlined and efficient system for the repatriation of deceased expatriates to ensure dignity for the dead and peace for the mind for the grieving families.
caption:
Bringing a loved one home for the last time is already painful, but for many Bangladeshi expatriates' families, it is becoming a nightmare.

Families of deceased expatriates are facing extreme difficulties and endless suffering while trying to bring the bodies of their loved ones back to Bangladesh.

The process of repatriation involves navigating complex bureaucratic hurdles and coordinating between different government agencies and embassies.

Families often report delays in the paperwork and a lack of clear guidance on the necessary legal requirements for transporting remains across borders.

These logistical challenges add significant emotional distress to families who are already grieving the loss of a member.

The situation highlights the need for a more streamlined and efficient system for the repatriation of deceased expatriates to ensure dignity for the dead and peace for the mind for the grieving families.

#Bangladesh #Expatriates #Repatriation #HumanRights #News

Source: Somoy News
